title: Orsen and the Autopsy
premise: When estate lawyer Casper Nystrom is handed a will for a woman officially declared dead five years ago, she assumes a clerical error — until the woman's diary, entered into evidence, contains dated entries written after her disappearance, including one describing Casper's own arrival in town. Following the diary's trail, Casper discovers that the missing woman, Lena Voss, faked her death to escape a thirty-year-old cover-up involving the town's founding families, and that someone is now killing off the witnesses. As the statute of limitations on the original crime expires, Casper must choose between protecting the client who trusts her and exposing a truth that implicates her own late father. The novel ends with Casper testifying at Lena's quiet resurrection hearing, having traded the town's comfortable silence for the truth — and finding, for the first time, that she can live with the mess.
about_author: August Joubert is the pen name of a former probate clerk from the upper Midwest who spent a decade filing wills for people who preferred not to be found. This is the second novel in the Casper Nystrom series.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Casper Nystrom, meticulous and emotionally walled-off, opens a probate file for Lena Voss — declared dead five years ago — and finds a freshly notarized will. The notary stamp belongs to a man who died last winter. POV Casper. Beat: unease disguised as professional irritation.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Grief
chapters.summary: Casper reviews her five years of estate files and notices three other cases with anomalies she'd filed away as errors — all connected to the same families. Her assistant, Dev, gently suggests she's projecting. POV Casper. Beat: the first crack in her ordered world.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: The court releases Lena Voss's diary as evidence. Casper reads entries dated weeks after the disappearance, the handwriting unmistakably Lena's. The final entry mentions 'the Nystrom girl' arriving in town. POV Casper, with diary excerpts. Beat: cold dread — she is inside the story.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Isn't
chapters.summary: Casper interviews Lena's brother, Anders, who insists his sister is dead and begs her to drop the file. His alibi for the disappearance week is suspiciously detailed, rehearsed. POV Casper. Beat: loyalty and fear braided together.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Casper visits the reservoir where Lena's car was found. A retired deputy, Hal Brandt, lets slip that the dive report was rewritten. He asks her, oddly, how her father is. POV Casper. Beat: the past reaching for her personally.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Lena's diary POV, 1994: a young Lena witnesses something at the Voss family mill — an accidental death covered up by the town's founders, her father among them. Beat: the original sin revealed to the reader before the protagonist.

chapters.title: The Client
chapters.summary: Casper receives a letter, hand-delivered, from Lena Voss — alive, in hiding, asking Casper to execute the will only if she fails to return before the statute expires. Casper meets her at a motel. POV Casper. Beat: the case becomes real, and so does the danger.

chapters.title: Dev Finds a Pattern
chapters.summary: Dev, digging through archived newspapers, maps the 1994 cover-up to four founding families — including a Nystrom. Casper forbids him to continue, then secretly photocopies his notes. POV Dev. Beat: Casper's loyalty to her father's memory begins to war with truth.

chapters.title: The Second Death
chapters.summary: Hal Brandt is found dead in his boat, ruled an accident. His dive report copy is missing. Casper realizes the witnesses are being erased in the order they'd testify. POV Casper. Beat: the mystery turns lethal; the clock is now visible.

chapters.title: Alibi, 1994
chapters.summary: Casper interviews the surviving founders, now elderly, whose alibis for the night of the mill death are identical in phrasing — clearly coached. One, Margaret Ellery, slips and calls Lena 'that child.' POV Casper. Beat: the wall of complicity takes shape.

chapters.title: Father's Files
chapters.summary: Casper breaks into her late father's storage unit and finds his own copy of the mill incident report — annotated, and with a page torn out. She remembers, painfully, how he changed after 1994. POV Casper, memory interleaved. Beat: grief weaponized against her.

chapters.title: The Diary Continues
chapters.summary: A second diary surfaces, mailed anonymously to the courthouse — entries up to last month, naming the person Lena fears most. The handwriting is right, but the paper is wrong. POV Casper and Dev. Beat: doubt — is Lena being framed, or framing someone?

chapters.title: Margaret's Bargain
chapters.summary: Margaret Ellery offers Casper a deal: the torn page from her father's file in exchange for Lena leaving town forever. She reveals Casper's father helped stage the disappearance to protect Lena. POV Casper. Beat: the ground shifts — her father was protector, not perpetrator.

chapters.title: Anders Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted with the coached alibis, Anders confesses his sister is alive and that he helped her vanish — but insists he doesn't know who killed Hal. His fear is of someone still in town. POV Casper and Anders. Beat: sympathy deepens; suspicion narrows.

chapters.title: The Statute
chapters.summary: Casper calculates the timeline: the 1994 obstruction charge expires in eleven days. Lena wants to come back and testify; the killer wants the file buried. Dev is followed home. POV Dev. Beat: stakes made explicit and personal.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Casper trades Margaret's page against her own better judgment and finds it names the actual driver in the 1994 death — the town's beloved current mayor, Ruth Calloway. POV Casper. Beat: the revelation lands, but the source is compromised.

chapters.title: Trap at the Reservoir
chapters.summary: Lena agrees to retrieve her original diaries from a cache near the reservoir; someone tips off the killer. Casper and Lena are ambushed at night; they escape when Dev arrives with police. POV Casper. Beat: climax of physical danger; allies proven.

chapters.title: Ruth's Version
chapters.summary: Mayor Calloway, cornered, tells her side: the death was an accident, the cover-up was collective, and she's spent thirty years buying the town's prosperity with its silence. She offers Casper a partnership in that silence. POV Casper and Ruth. Beat: the seduction of complicity at its strongest.

chapters.title: What Casper Knows
chapters.summary: Casper discovers her father didn't just protect Lena — he kept the full evidence all along, waiting for someone brave enough to use it. The missing page was his test. POV Casper, memory interleaved. Beat: reconciliation with the dead; resolve hardens.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Casper files everything: the diaries, the rewritten dive report, the coached alibis, her father's evidence. The town erupts; Margaret recants her deal; Ruth's lawyer moves to suppress. POV Casper. Beat: the point of no return, professionally and personally.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Lena Voss testifies at the hearing to reverse her declared death, with Ruth Calloway's prosecution proceeding on the 1994 obstruction charge before the statute lapses. Casper takes the stand and names her father's role without flinching. POV Casper. Beat: climax — truth spoken aloud, at cost.

chapters.title: Filed Under V
chapters.summary: Weeks later: Ruth pleads down, the town simmers, Anders and Lena reconcile awkwardly. Casper reshelves her files — and leaves one drawer deliberately unalphabetized, a small rebellion against the order she hid behind. POV Casper. Beat: quiet resolution; identity remade by truth.
